stem: At the beginning of a shift, the interprofessional team leader wants to review the patient care plan, identify team members and roles, establish goals, and anticipate likely contingencies. Which TeamSTEPPS tool is most appropriate?
rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS defines a brief as a short session used before care or at the start of a work period to share the plan, discuss team formation, assign roles and responsibilities, establish expectations and goals, and anticipate outcomes or contingencies. Therefore A is correct. A huddle is an ad hoc meeting used during care to reassess the plan or situational awareness. A debrief occurs after or following team performance to identify lessons and improve future performance. A check-back is a closed-loop communication technique rather than a team-planning meeting.
educational_objective: Select the TeamSTEPPS brief when a team leader needs to establish the team, clarify roles and goals, share the care plan, and anticipate contingencies before care or at the start of a shift.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: TeamSTEPPS 3.0 — Module 2 Team Leadership: Overview of Key Concepts and Tools; Sharing the Care Plan: Brief
source_version_date: TeamSTEPPS 3.0 updated 2023; Team Leadership overview last reviewed May 2023; Brief page last reviewed December 2023; curriculum index last reviewed October 2024
source_locator: Module 2 Team Leadership > Ensuring Coordinated Team Activities > Sharing the Patient Care Plan — Brief; Sharing the Care Plan: Brief > team membership/roles, clinical status, care plan, team operations, goals and expectations; Huddle and Debrief definitions in same module
source_claim_supported: TeamSTEPPS uses a brief to establish team membership, roles, goals, expectations, and the care plan before or at the start of care; huddles reassess the plan during care, debriefs review performance, and check-backs are communication tools.

correction_summary: Replaced a generic values-based collaboration item with a concrete TeamSTEPPS leadership-tool decision. The final item distinguishes brief, huddle, debrief, and check-back using their exact functions and is more directly testable and nursing-relevant. Correct option changed from C to A; difficulty reduced from hard to easy.
